## What you take with you {#what-you-take-with-you .smaller}

::: {.small}
- **Yours now**: a reproduced result, and what it rests on; an estimand statement and a causal graph that you wrote yourself; your results on the class chart, with a reason for each choice
- **Read**: the three *Nature* 2026 papers [@MiskeEtAl2026InvestigatingReproducibilitySocial; @AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness; @TynerEtAl2026InvestigatingReplicabilitySocial]; the glossary [@NosekEtAl2025BriefGlossaryTerms]; @LundbergEtAl2021WhatYourEstimand; on colliders and selection, @ColeEtAl2010IllustratingBiasDue and @GriffithEtAl2020ColliderBiasUndermines; on discrete-time event-history models, @Allison1982DiscreteTimeMethodsEvent; the paper itself [@KuoRaley2016DivergingPatternsUnion]
- **Explore**: the case study, the decision map and the companion module on event-history analysis on the course site; the NSFG pages of the National Center for Health Statistics; the SCORE dossier on the OSF
- **Keep going locally**: the research-software and open-research teams at your university, or a ReproducibiliTea journal club near you
- Everything is on the course site, and everything is open – fork any of it
:::

::: notes
You take home a reproduced result, and an understanding of what it does and does not establish, an estimand statement and a causal graph that you wrote for a real published claim, and your results on the class chart, each with a reason. The reading list on the slide is short on purpose: the three Nature papers on reproduction, robustness and replication, the glossary that gave us the grid, the paper on estimands, two short papers on what conditioning on a collider does, Allison on discrete-time event-history models, and the original paper. The course site has the case study, the decision map, the companion module on event-history analysis and the full public record. And two pointers for keeping the habit alive: most universities have a research-software team and an open-research or library data service, and ReproducibiliTea journal clubs meet in many cities.
:::
